summary: Nodearr's copyright notice credits Sonarr, Prowlarr and Nodearr's contributors each for their own years, and `usage.nodearr.com` can't be flooded from one machine. Nodes on 0.10.0 and later hear of this release by themselves and, where they can, install it.

changes.heading: Changed
items: `usage.nodearr.com` turns away a third report sent within 10 seconds from the same address, so one machine can't flood it. Cloudflare does the counting before the service runs, so the service still never reads addresses. A node sends one report every 6 hours and never meets the limit ([Privacy and security](https://github.com/Nodearr/Nodearr/blob/v0.11.1/docs/user-guide/privacy-and-security.md#anonymous-usage-report), [ADR 0024](https://github.com/Nodearr/Nodearr/blob/v0.11.1/docs/adr/0024-update-checks-and-usage-reports-on-nodearr-com.md#2026-11-10-a-rate-limit-for-usage-reports)).

changes.heading: Fixed
items: The copyright notice in Nodearr's program files gives Sonarr, Prowlarr and Nodearr's contributors each their own years, and names Prowlarr, whose code Nodearr also contains: `Copyright 2014-2026 sonarr.tv; Copyright 2014-2026 prowlarr.com; Copyright 2026 Nodearr's contributors`. It had given Sonarr and Nodearr's contributors one range ending in the year of the build, and left Prowlarr out. `NOTICE.md` now records Prowlarr's notice beside Sonarr's ([NOTICE.md](https://github.com/Nodearr/Nodearr/blob/v0.11.1/NOTICE.md#assembly-copyright)).
